title: Biological Approach Adventure 1: Brain Regions
welcome_lead: Today you'll tour the brain lobes, the amygdala and the hippocampus.

walkthroughs.body_html:
The cortex divides into four lobes.

Frontal — planning, decision-making, personality (Phineas Gage 1848).
Parietal — somatosensation, spatial reasoning.
Temporal — hearing, language (Wernicke's area), memory.
Occipital — vision.

Deeper structures regulate emotion and memory.

Amygdala — almond-shaped; processes fear and emotional memory (LeDoux 1996).
Hippocampus — encodes new long-term memories. Patient HM (Milner 1957) lost his hippocampi and could form no new declarative memories.

Brain function is studied via:

- Lesion studies (HM, Gage).
- fMRI — blood-oxygen activity.
- EEG — electrical waves.
- PET — radioactive tracer.

Maguire et al. (2000) used MRI to show London taxi drivers had a larger posterior hippocampus — neuroplasticity in action.
